title: A cyclotron and its field
hook: Change magnetic-field magnitude and predict cyclotron frequency.
misconception: cyclotron frequency stays fixed when magnetic-field magnitude doubles.
objective: Apply f = abs(q)B/(2πm) to compare cyclotron frequency when magnetic-field magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a nonrelativistic particle with fixed mass and charge moving perpendicular to a uniform field, f = abs(q)B/(2πm). When magnetic-field magnitude doubles, cyclotron frequency becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model f = abs(q)B/(2πm); scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a nonrelativistic particle with fixed mass and charge moving perpendicular to a uniform field, with a nonzero initial result. If magnetic-field magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on cyclotron frequency?
recall.why: Apply f = abs(q)B/(2πm) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
